status: Research intermediate; design_inference fields are proposals, not verified Deep Primal features.

sources.title: Houdini Heightfields and terrains
sources.inspected: Overview, limitations, scale/resolution, named layers and masks; page served as Houdini 22.0 documentation.
sources.limits: A two-dimensional surface document does not establish volumetric topology, conserved material quantities, or a runtime voxel editing system.

sources.title: Houdini HeightField Erode 3.0
sources.inspected: Solver, masks, feature scale, layer bindings, freeze/cache behavior; node is documented as introduced in Houdini 21.0.
sources.limits: Visual similarity is not bitwise determinism or mass conservation. The inspected reference is Erode 3.0, not its older namesake.

sources.title: Gaea Tiled Builds
sources.inspected: Tiled/full differences, world/detail separation, hybrid buckets, blending, and data-map import.
sources.limits: An authoring overlap recommendation is not proof of deterministic independent chunk generation or a conserved cross-tile water simulation.

sources.title: Gaea Stratify
sources.inspected: Description and controls for spacing, octaves, strength, shape, seed, tilt, and orientation.
sources.limits: No evidence here establishes physical stratigraphic age, groundwater behavior, ore distributions, or consistent lithology through an excavated volume.

sources.title: World Machine Professional Edition Addendum — tiling
sources.inspected: Tiled output, shared edge vertices, subsets, coordinate naming, orientation, and context-sensitive simulation caveats.
sources.limits: This is an old addendum with obsolete platform references. No current product limits, speed, thread counts, or recommended tile sizes are inferred.

sources.title: Unreal Engine — Using PCG Generation Modes
sources.inspected: Partitioned/hierarchical generation, coarse-to-fine data, duplicate point handling, runtime sources, cleanup radius, and scheduler controls.
sources.limits: PCG mesh generation does not establish a voxel authority model, save transaction semantics, or cross-platform deterministic world generation.

sources.title: Unreal Engine World Partition
sources.inspected: Spatial cell lifecycle, actor dependencies, streaming sources, loaded/activated states, teleport preparation, and debug/parallel-load controls.
sources.limits: The inspected page concerns Unreal actor/cell management, not transactional mutable voxel terrain. Its default spatial policy is not adopted automatically.

sources.title: Godot Voxel Tools — Generators
sources.inspected: Generator API, density fields, multipass dependencies/determinism/limits, modifiers, and output caching.
sources.limits: Some page sections are historical; implementation capability needs a pinned revision. The documented multipass column method does not directly provide arbitrary-LOD generation.

sources.title: Godot Voxel Tools — Streams
sources.inspected: Chunk saves, modified/generated output policy, asynchronous completion, world switching, resource lifetime, and forced shutdown.
sources.limits: Asynchronous chunk persistence does not itself guarantee atomic multi-chunk terrain edits, exactly-once transfers, or crash-safe composition accounting.

sources.title: GeoClaw description and contents
sources.inspected: Model scope, topography, dry cells, wetting/drying, moving terrain and parameter/reference navigation.
sources.limits: Depth averaging cannot establish general three-dimensional cave flow, pressurized plumbing, air entrainment, or composition transport.

sources.title: Berger, George, LeVeque and Mandli — GeoClaw depth-averaged flows with adaptive refinement
sources.inspected: Sections 2–5: conservation variables, equilibrium, wet/dry interfaces, refinement/time stepping, restriction and topography integration.
sources.limits: This is a 2011 model/method paper, not a claim about today's code. Its scientific approximation and reservoir assumptions differ from finite game accounts.

sources.title: Barnes, Lehman and Mulla — Priority-Flood
sources.inspected: Algorithms 1–2 and sections 3, 4 and 7: depression treatment, queue ordering, NoData, flow directions and watershed labels.
sources.limits: This is a complete-domain elevation algorithm, not a three-dimensional finite-water solver or a guarantee that arbitrary chunk-local drainage is globally consistent.
